title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: DKA

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 56 y/o female with hx of T2DM admitted with acute ketoacidosis. Pt presented with polyuria, polydipsia, and fatigue. On arrival, pt was alert and oriented. Labs confirmed metabolic acidosis and elevated ketones. Initiated aggressive fluid resuscitation and continuous insulin drip. Pt responded well to treatment; electrolytes stabilized and acid-base balance normalized. Pt tolerated oral intake well during stay. Vital signs stable, RRR, CTAB. No acute distress. Plan included education on glucose monitoring and insulin titration.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Diabetic ketoacidosis
- Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
- Insulin glargine subcutaneous daily
- Metformin 500mg BID
- Lisinopril 10mg daily

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for lab work and titration of insulin regimen. Pt instructed to call clinic if symptoms of hyperglycemia recur.

Electronically signed
D. Kowalski, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with ketoacidosis without coma: E11.10 (HCC 36).

distractors.why: Ketoacidosis is a severe acute complication (HCC 36).
